app.title: middleware
common.copyFailed: Copy failed — select it by hand
keys.title: Keyboard shortcuts
keys.new: New (site, task, token…) on screens that create things
keys.escape: Close a dialog, leave a field
spark.label: Requests per second: now {now}, peak {max}
auth.loginLead: Sign in with the operator password of this installation.
auth.setupLead: This installation has no operator yet. Run `middleware setup` on the server to get a one-time code.
auth.codeHint: Printed by `middleware setup` on the server.
auth.passwordHint: At least 8 characters. There is no reset by email: keep it somewhere safe.
auth.wrong: That did not work. Check the password and try again.
auth.firstRun: First run? Set up the operator
auth.expired: Your session ended. Sign in again.
sites.domainHint: The folder sites/<domain>/ is created with a manifest from the template.
sites.templateHint: Only the starting manifest; everything can be changed afterwards.
sites.badDomain: That does not look like a domain.
sites.randomHint: Make up a name from words you can say out loud. What the field holds is kept as the parent domain.
sites.emptyHint: Create one, or put a folder with a site.json under sites/.
modules.desc.openspec: Spec-driven development: before a change is built, the agent writes what and why, and someone approves it. New sites are set up for it, and each site shows its specs and changes in a Specs tab.
specs.hint: What the project says it does (specs) and what is being changed (changes). The agent proposes; you approve here or in the chat.
specs.noChanges: None. Ask the agent in the chat to propose one.
specs.noSpecs: None yet: they appear when the first change is archived.
specs.offHint: Enable it under Modules: it installs its CLI and sets new sites up.
specs.noneTitle: This project does not use OpenSpec
specs.noneHint: Creates the openspec/ folder and OpenSpec's skills for the agents. Touches nothing else.
specs.applyBody: The site's agent is asked, in its chat, to build it following its tasks. You will see it work there and can stop it.
specs.archiveBody: Its changes become the project's specs and it is no longer in progress.
specs.applyMsg: Approved: build the OpenSpec change “{id}” with its apply workflow (openspec-apply-change), ticking each task in tasks.md once it is done and checked.
specs.archiveMsg: Archive the OpenSpec change “{id}” (openspec archive {id} --yes) if all its tasks are done and the site works, and commit.
site.goneHint: It was deleted or archived while you were looking at it.
site.stopBody: Visitors get the “stopped” page until you start it again. The process is ended; the files stay.
site.holdBody: Visitors see a holding page with this title and message. No process runs while held.
site.deleteBody: It is unpublished first: its tunnel routes and the DNS records that point at this house are removed. Then the site stops answering.
site.archiveHint: The folder moves to data/archive/ and can be restored by hand. Unchecked, it is deleted for good.
site.adoptBody: Writes a site.json into the folder so the middleware starts serving it.
site.unmanagedNotice: This folder has no site.json, so it is not served. Adopt it to write one.
site.envHint: What the running instance was born with. Secrets are masked. Changes to the manifest apply at the next handover.
site.envEmpty: No instance is running, so there is nothing resolved.
manifest.hint: site.json as the engine reads it. Saving validates it; a change to run, env or runtime triggers a handover.
manifest.changedUnderneath: The manifest changed on disk at {at} while you were editing. Reload to see it; saving overwrites.
editor.label: JSON editor
logs.label: Log output
files.pickHint: Text files can be edited here. Anything else is shown read-only.
files.tooBigHint: {size}; use the shell for this one.
chat.placeholder: Ask the agent to change something in this site…
chat.waitUpload: Waiting for the files to upload
chat.newBody: Its turns are deleted and the next message starts from nothing. To keep it and talk about something else, open another conversation instead.
chat.emptyHint: The agent works inside this site's folder and nowhere else.
chat.capacityTitle: Agent turns running on this machine, of the cap set in Settings
chat.capacityFull: Every agent slot is taken ({used} of {max}). The message was not sent: try again when a turn ends, or raise the cap in Settings.
access.title: Access
access.hint: Who may reach this site. Applied live, no restart.
access.passwordHint: Basic auth for the whole site. Leave empty for none.
access.allowHint: One IP or CIDR per line. Empty allows everyone.
access.wafOffHint: No rate limit and no body limit. The block list and the bans for exploits, scanners and failed logins still apply: they protect the whole machine.
inbound.sub: Three doors into this machine: a tunnel, the public ports, and the local bench.
inbound.localDetail: The development bench: plain HTTP on this machine and a name server that resolves every site here. No internet, no hosts file.
inbound.localHelp: How to point this machine's resolver here
inbound.tunnelDetail: A reverse tunnel pushes to the loopback port. No public IP, no certificates here.
inbound.portsDetail: Listening on {http} and {https} with certificates from ACME.
inbound.closeBody: Domains that come in by it stop answering. The panel stays reachable through the other door.
inbound.doorFailed: The door did not change; see the lines
inbound.certAuto: Expires {expires}. Renewed automatically from {renews} (30 days before).
inbound.emptyHint: Sites appear here once they exist.
inbound.moveFailed: Some domains did not move; see the lines
waf.sub: Always on. Rate limits, blocking and under-attack mode for the whole machine.
waf.noTraffic: No requests in the last minute.
waf.policyHint: Applies to every site unless its manifest says otherwise.
waf.underAttackHint: Challenges every visitor of every site. Switches immediately.
waf.noneBlockedHint: Addresses that trip the limits show up here, and you can block one by hand.
modules.sub: What not every installation wants. Enabling verifies before it saves.
modules.disableBody: Credentials are kept; enable again to resume.
modules.forgetBody: They are removed from disk. You will have to enter them again.
modules.notInstalled: Enabled, but its binary is not installed. Enable again to install it.
modules.sessionNone: not signed in: the CLI's own login under each site's home is used
modules.signInStarting: Starting the sign-in on the server…
modules.signInStep1: Open the link on any device and authorize:
modules.signInStep2: Paste the code it gives you here.
modules.binaryMissing: {name} is not installed yet; enabling or signing in installs it.
modules.binaryManaged: installed and kept current by this installation
settings.depsHint: The agent CLIs come from npm and have releases of their own. The installation checks daily for a newer one.
tasks.sub: Scheduled work, one JSON file each under tasks/.
tasks.name: Name
tasks.nameHint: Lower-case letters, digits and dashes. Becomes tasks/<name>.json.
tasks.jsonHint: schedule is cron; site runs it in that site's folder; overlap is skip or queue.
tasks.emptyHint: A task runs a command on a schedule, optionally inside a site.
tasks.col.name: Task
tasks.deleteBody: The file is removed; a run in progress finishes.
events.sub: Everything that changed state, as it happens.
events.emptyHint: Nothing matches the filters, or nothing has happened yet.
events.col.subject: Subject
guard.sub: Rules cut first; a model is only asked afterwards.
settings.panelDomainHint: Where this console answers. Empty means loopback only.
settings.listenHint: The loopback address the tunnel pushes to.
settings.portsHint: Instances get a port from this range. Reserve it from the kernel's ephemeral range on the server.
settings.portsBad: The range must be two ports with the first below the second.
settings.saved: Settings saved. Some take effect at the next restart.
settings.pagesHint: What a visitor reads when a site is not there, stopped, held or down.
settings.pagesSaveHint: Saved with the Save button above.
settings.tokensHint: Bearer tokens for scripts and CI. The CLI on the server needs none.
settings.tokenNameHint: What uses it, so you know which one to revoke.
settings.noTokensHint: Create one for a script or a CI job.
settings.revokeBody: Whatever uses it stops working now.
settings.tokenOnce: This is the only time it is shown. Copy it now.
settings.languageHint: Add a file under i18n/ to add one.
settings.agentsHint: Every turn is an agent process with a model behind it. The cap is for the whole machine; the reserved slots keep the installation's own conversation answering when every site is busy.
settings.reservedForHouseHint: Slots only the middleware conversation may take. Below the cap.
settings.perProviderHint: 0 means no cap of its own.
settings.defaultProviderHint: For a site whose manifest names none.
settings.siteDailyUSDHint: What a site may spend a day through its Claude door when its manifest sets no daily_usd. Empty: 5.
settings.agentsBad: The cap must be 1 to 64, the reserved slots fewer than the cap, and a provider's cap 0 to 64.
settings.agentsSaved: Agent limits saved and in force.
system.noProcessesHint: No site is running a process right now.
system.update.title: Updates
system.update.installBody: The new release is downloaded from GitHub and checked against its sha256, then middleware restarts. Sites keep running and are re-adopted; WebSockets open through the proxy are cut. This console reconnects by itself.
system.update.autoHint: On, a new version found by a check is installed and the middleware restarts by itself; the sites keep running. Off, it is only announced and waits for «Update now».
system.update.why.not_release: This build is not a release, so it is not updated from here.
system.update.why.no_helper: There is no privileged helper (installed with --no-helper, or in a container): update with the install script.
system.restartBody: Sites keep running and are re-adopted. Open WebSockets through the proxy drop. This console reconnects by itself.
sites.publishHint: Points every name of the site at this house through the door for new sites: DNS, the tunnel's route or a certificate. A name without a dot is a project and is not published.
sites.importV1Body: Brings a site or app from another server (a V1 house or any other: pm2, systemd, Docker…) with its folder, its database if it lives inside and, from V1, its HOME. This house makes a permission that only receives that site and expires in 2 hours; the other server gets no other key.
sites.importV1BaseHint: Empty: this node's panel domain. If this node has none of its own, import into one that does and then use “Move to another node”.
sites.importV1Run: Run this on the server it is on now, with <the app's folder> replaced by its folder (in a V1 house: <V1 root>/sites/<domain>). If it is not V1, add --stop "…" and --start "…" with how it is stopped and started there (pm2, systemd…), and --command "…" if its folder does not say how it starts. Valid until {when}.
sites.importV1After: It is copied while it serves, its dependencies installed here, stopped for a few seconds for the last copy, and started. Once it answers here its names are pointed at this house by themselves (with the DNS provider on; otherwise they wait in Publish). If it does not start here, it is started there again and its names are not touched.
site.unpublishBody: Its tunnel routes and the DNS records that point at this house are removed. The site keeps running here.
publish.takeoverBody: In the zone, {name} already points somewhere else: {found}. Going on replaces that record and {name} serves {site}; whatever it pointed at stops getting visits through that name.
publish.conflictSays: It already points somewhere else: {found}. Nothing was changed.
inbound.publishingDetail: Where new sites are published, and the address the ports door is reached at. Empty detects it.
inbound.publicIPHint: Used for the A records of the ports door. Empty detects it each time it is needed.
inbound.retried: Retrying every name that is not published
site.holdUntilHint: Optional. Shown on the page and sent as Retry-After.
chat.exportHint: Download this conversation, every turn with its steps and its subagents', to hand to someone to read
chat.exportEmpty: Nothing to export yet: send a first message.
chat.processesBody: The turn and whatever it started, also what it left running on purpose with setsid (a build, a server). Nothing here is killed on its own.
site.downloadHint: The folder as a zip, without node_modules, builds and caches (they come back with an install or a build)
site.renameBody: The folder, its HOME, logs, conversations and cost move to the new name. The site stops for a moment; published names are taken down and the new ones published on the same door.
site.giveDomainBody: The project is renamed after the domain: its folder, its HOME, its conversations and its cost come along. It stops for a moment.
site.domainsHint: The names this site answers to. Each extra domain is published and certified like its own; if the zone already points it somewhere else, it stops and asks before touching it.
site.domainRemoveBody: It stops answering {name} and this house's DNS records for it are taken down.
site.domainsSaved: Saved; the names are published in a moment
site.redirectsHint: A request that comes in by “from” is sent to “to” with that code, before the site is served (stopped too). “from” is a path (/old), a prefix (/blog/*) or one of the site's names (alias.com/*); when “to” ends in /* the rest of the path is kept. The first that matches wins.
site.uncontainBody: It runs on the machine as a normal process: the same command in the same folder, without Docker. If the command needs Node and the machine has none, it is installed with nvm. It loses the container's isolation: it sees what the house's user sees. The container's settings are kept in case you go back.
site.uncontained: Out of the container; it restarts
site.containizeBody: The house looks for the image its command needs (its Dockerfile, or Node, Python or the machine's distribution, by what it starts with) and tries it beside the site, on another port, without stopping it. Only if it answers is it written in the manifest, and the site moves into the container without losing a request. If it cannot, the agent you pick is asked in a new conversation of the site: it writes the Dockerfile, and pressing this button again has the house build and try it the same way. This machine needs Docker working.
site.containAgent: If the house cannot on its own, ask
site.containStep.trying: Trying it in a container beside the site
site.containStep.done: In the container; the site hands over without a cut
site.containStep.asked: The house could not on its own and asked the agent
site.containStep.failed: It could not be put in a container
site.moveBody: It is copied while it serves; then it stops for a few seconds for the last copy with whatever changed, starts on the other node, and its names point there by themselves. If it does not start there, it runs here again as it was. The copy here is archived.
site.moveStep.check: Asking {node} whether it can take it
site.moveStep.repair: The house's AI looks at it on {node}
moves.background: It goes on in the background even if you close this or reload.
moves.warnSay: It runs on the other node, with warnings: see the details.
moves.failedBack: It failed, and the site runs here again as it was.
doctor.title: Machine checks
doctor.hint: What `middleware doctor` says on the server: the binary, the units, the loopback socket, the helper, the root, the reserved ports, docker, fail2ban, Node, wireguard and the disk. It only reads.
req.title: The house's requirements
req.hint: Installs what this machine is missing for everything to work: git, curl, WireGuard and nftables; Docker, with your user in its group; fail2ban with the house's jail; nvm with Node's LTS and, if ticked, a headless Chromium for the site pictures. The house's helper does it as root, in a unit of its own: it does not touch the house's configuration or restart it, and installs nothing outside that list.
req.browser: Also install Chromium when missing (over 100 MB)
req.runQ: Install what this machine is missing?
req.runBody: Only the packages on the list are installed, with the machine's package manager. It can take a few minutes; it goes on if you close the panel.
req.background: It goes on in the background even if you close this or reload.
req.state.restart: Done: restart the house for it to use Docker
leftovers.title: What moves left
leftovers.hint: What moves left on this node: receptions that never finished, earlier copies of a site's data set aside to make room for what arrived (one per attempt, each a whole HOME), and sites placed here that never started. Nothing is removed unless you tick it.
leftovers.none: Moves left nothing on this node.
leftovers.cleanBody: They are removed from this node's disk. A placed site that never started is taken out as the move would have: what arrived out, and what was there before under that name, back.
dash.networkOnlyHint: Take its panel off its domain: it is managed from the network's panels alone
dash.networkOnlyBody: Its panel leaves {domain}: its DNS record and route are retired and it is no longer reached from the internet. It is managed from any other node's panel, as now. Undone by giving it a domain again in its Settings.
dash.networkOnlyBodyHere: You are on this node's own panel, at {domain}: this page stops answering once you confirm. Its DNS record and route are retired and it is managed from another node's panel. Undone by giving it a domain again in its Settings, from the network.
dash.networkOnlyDone: {name} is managed from the network only now ({from})
live.purgeBody: Every conversation the panel holds, of every site and of the house, goes with its attachments and cannot be recovered. One at work stays; the ones a site's code opened through its door stay too, and what was spent is still counted.
live.purgeBodyNodes: Every conversation the panel holds on all {n} nodes, of every site and of the house, goes with its attachments and cannot be recovered. One at work stays; the ones a site's code opened through its door stay too, and what was spent is still counted.
access.zonesHint: Paths with their own password or address list, on top of the above. Protect /admin alone and the rest of the site stays open. "/admin" covers /admin and everything under it (not /administrator); when two zones match, the longer wins.
access.zonesNone: No zones: the rules above apply to the whole site.
access.zoneKeep: Leave empty to keep the current one
access.zoneAllowHint: One per line (IP or CIDR range). Empty: from anywhere.
access.zoneEmpty: The zone {path} protects nothing: give it a password or an address list, or remove it
plan.title: What it will do
plan.installs: Installs its dependencies there, for that machine, in:
plan.nodePinned: Runs here on Node {v}: written in its manifest so it runs on the same there
plan.docker: It runs in a container: the target needs Docker
plan.names: Points its names at the target: {names}
automation.title: The house's AI for automatic work
automation.hint: Who works when nobody is watching: it repairs a site that arrives from a move and does not start (before the move is undone, with the site stopped at the source for a few minutes at most), looks after recently arrived sites that go down during their first day even with the automatic repairs off, and makes the automatic repairs. It has nothing to do with the house's agent, where you pick whom you talk to each time. With none, none of this happens.
moves.title: Moves
moves.hint: They go on in the background even with the panel closed. Each step, with its state, how long it took and, if it failed, why.
site.moveStep.install: Installing its dependencies on {node}, for that machine, while it serves here
site.moveStep.export: Exporting its workers' data here, stopped
site.moveStep.start: Waiting for it to answer on {node}
sites.archivedBody: Each is one file with everything the folder had, data and dependencies included. Restoring puts it back in sites/ as it was.
chat.siteDoorNote: This conversation was opened by the site's own code through the site door. It can be read and stopped here, not written into.
claudeUse.sub: What each site's code spent through its Claude door. Days are UTC, like the caps.
claudeUse.none: No site has spent anything yet
claudeUse.noneHint: Open a site's Claude door from its page and its code can ask Claude through the house.
door.title: AI gateway
door.hint: The site's own code can ask an AI through the house: the agent and model chosen here, the same jail, the cost counted, and its conversations visible here. Its process gets MIDDLEWARE_TOKEN and MIDDLEWARE_API.
door.noProcess: This site serves files: it has no process of its own that could call the gateway.
door.openBody: The site restarts so its process gets its token. It starts on Claude (or the first agent available), with every permission and the house's daily cap; all of it can be changed after.
door.closeBody: The site restarts without its token, and its calls are refused from now on. Its conversations are kept.
door.agentHint: The ones whose module is enabled and that can run now.
door.noAgents: No AI agent is available: enable one under Modules.
door.permHint.read: Reads the site's folder; without changing files or commands, never its .env.
door.permHint.edit: Creates and changes files in the site's folder.
door.permHint.web: Searches and reads the web. A document could try to carry data out in a URL.
door.permHint.shell: Runs commands in the site's folder, behind the house's jail. With commands it can also read and reach the network.
door.fixed.openai.shell: Codex reads and changes files through its terminal: commands come with reading or changing files (read-only if it only reads), and with neither it has no terminal.
door.fixed.agy.web: Antigravity's web search cannot be taken away: it always has it. Without Internet, reading pages and the browser are closed.
door.fixed.other: “{perm}” cannot be taken away on its own with this agent.
door.turnsHint: For agents on a subscription, whose turns do not say what they cost. 0 is no cap (Claude); the others get 200 when it is left empty.
door.raiseBody: The site's process answers the internet: whoever manages to make it ask something gets these permissions. Give them only if the site needs them.
door.modelHint: The one used when a call names none.
door.modelsHint: Tick several and the app picks one per call with "model" (a cheap one to classify, a strong one to write). Asking for one not ticked is a 400. None ticked: any of the agent's.
door.dailyHint: Checked before every call; past it, the call gets 429 until tomorrow (UTC).
door.maxChatsHint: At the limit the oldest go, never one at work.
door.hide: Keep its conversations out of the panel's list
door.forDevelopers: For whoever writes the site's code
door.envHint: These reach the site's process as environment variables; a container gets the socket mounted at the same path.
vpn.title: VPN
vpn.off: The VPN is off. Turn it on under Modules; it asks nothing.
vpn.on: On. Devices connect to {endpoint}; this server is {address} inside it.
vpn.noHelper: The privileged helper is not reachable: the interface cannot be brought up.
vpn.removeBody: Its key stops working at once; its file is useless from now on.
vpn.noDevicesHint: Add one and its WireGuard file downloads at once.
vpn.panelOnly: The panel only through the VPN
vpn.panelOnlyHint: Through the tunnel or ports 80/443 the panel then does not exist; from the machine itself (SSH) it stays reachable, the way back if a device is lost. Inside the VPN, open it with http:// if its certificate came through the tunnel.
vpn.panelOnlyQ: Put the panel inside the VPN?
vpn.panelOnlyBody: From now on the panel answers only to the devices of the VPN (and to the machine itself, over SSH). Check one of them connects before closing this tab.
vpn.panelOpenQ: Open the panel outside the VPN?
vpn.panelOpenBody: It answers again through the tunnel or ports 80/443, behind its password.
vpn.panelOnlyDone: The panel answers only through the VPN
vpn.panelOpenDone: The panel answers outside the VPN again
vpn.deviceNameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens: phone, laptop-ana…
vpn.onlyNow: The file has been downloaded. This is the only time it can be had: its key is not kept. If it is lost, remove the device and add it again.
vpn.howTo: Import it in the WireGuard app (desktop: Import tunnel from file; phone: + and Import from file). Only the VPN's traffic goes through it, and its DNS resolves this house's names.
vpn.siteHint: Whether this site, or some of its paths, answers only to the devices of the VPN. Through any other door it does not exist (404, as an unknown name).
vpn.siteNeedsVPN: Turn the VPN on under Modules to keep this site, or some paths of it, inside it.
vpn.mode.whole: Only the VPN: the whole site
vpn.mode.paths: Public, but these paths only through the VPN
vpn.pathsHint: One per line. /admin covers /admin and everything under it, not /administrator.
vpn.onlyDevicesHint: None ticked is every device of the VPN.
vpn.wholeQ: Keep all of {domain} inside the VPN?
vpn.wholeBody: It stops being published: its DNS records and tunnel route are taken down, and from outside the VPN it does not exist. When it leaves the VPN it is published again on the door it was on.
unrouted.title: Names without a site
unrouted.hint: Names that reached this house and no site serves. Through the tunnel it is usually a rule that outlived its site or a DNS record left behind; through the ports, mostly scanners trying a Host. Kept in memory since the last start.
unrouted.noneHint: Every name that arrived belongs to a site.
unrouted.name: Name
seen.title: Who calls
seen.hint: {n} requests counted since {since}, before the rules above (what they shut out is here too). What a rule is written from.
seen.forgetBody: It starts counting again from now, so the list says what calls today and not what stopped calling a month ago.
house.stopBody: The agent stops where it is; what it changed stays. What it left running in the background is listed under that conversation's processes.
vitals.title: The machine, live
vitals.hint: The last hour, a sample every 5 seconds. The dashed line is where a stretch under strain starts counting as an episode.
vitals.noEpisodes: None yet: the machine has not been under strain for more than 30 seconds.
vitals.blame: on top {times} times, {cpu} of a core
settings.pagePreview.down: A site that does not answer
settings.cacheHint: The memory every site's response cache shares. A site may ask for less in its manifest, never for more.
edge.pricesHint: Yearly price in USD of each ending, one per line (com 10.44). Written by hand: no registrar's API gives them for every ending. The search shows them, and warns when they are over six months old.
edge.pricesBad: This line does not read as an ending and a price: {line}
pages.themeNote.sober: The name large, a status band across the page, warm paper. The one that has always been served; fits almost anything.
pages.themeNote.card: A centred card on a tinted field, closer to an app than a notice. For what customers see.
pages.themeNote.console: Monospaced and dark, the state and code on top. For internal things and work in progress: the machine talking.
pages.themeNote.note: Almost nothing: a line, a rule and the words. For when the notice must not look designed: a parked domain.
pages.themeNote.poster: Flat ink, square edges, the label as a block and the HTTP code huge and faint behind everything. For a brand that speaks in posters.
pages.themeNote.blueprint: Dark blue grid paper, framing corners instead of a border, the explanation hanging from a leader line. A diagnosis, not an apology.
pages.themeNote.glitch: Black screen, scan lines, the title split in two offset copies like a badly tuned signal. For a game or a hardware project.
inbound.moveBackground: They are moved one at a time in the background (certificate, door, DNS each); you can close this and come back, and stop it between two domains.
inbound.migrationDone: Done: {done} of {total} on the {door} door, {failed} failed.
inbound.migrationCancelled: Stopped: {done} of {total} on the {door} door, {failed} failed.
inbound.migrationCancelling: It stops after the domain it is on
modules.desc.cloudflare: DNS records, tunnel routes, the edge's cache and Access, managed from the panel.
modules.desc.vpn: A WireGuard door to the panel and to the sites, one file per device.
modules.desc.github: Deploy on push: a webhook builds the site and hands over by pointer.
modules.desc.agent-claude: Conversations run by Claude Code. Sign in with your Claude subscription here, or give it an API key.
modules.desc.agent-agy: Conversations run by Google's Antigravity CLI. Sign in with your Google account here.
modules.needHelp.cloudflare.token: An API token with Zone:DNS:Edit on the zones to manage, and Account:Cloudflare Tunnel:Edit if a tunnel is used. Created at dash.cloudflare.com/profile/api-tokens.
modules.needHelp.cloudflare.account_id: Found when empty, if the token sees exactly one account.
modules.needHelp.cloudflare.tunnel_id: The tunnel this server runs, to publish through it. Empty is DNS only: sites are reached on 80 and 443. Never taken by itself: a tunnel of another server would split its traffic with this one.
modules.needHelp.github.webhook_secret: Generated when empty. Paste it in the repository's webhook settings, content type application/json, push events only.
modules.needHelp.github.token: For private repositories, a fine-grained token with Contents: Read on them; with Read and write, a site's conversation can also git push to the repository its manifest deploys from. Never written to disk in clear, and never shown to the conversation.
modules.needHelp.vpn.endpoint: Empty: this machine's public address, found by itself, with the port below.
modules.needHelp.agent-claude.model: Offered first in the panel. Empty: the first one listed.
modules.needHelp.agent-claude.api_key: Passed to the CLI as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Leave empty and sign in above to use your subscription.
modules.needHelp.agent-claude.bin: Path to the claude executable. Empty: the one this installation keeps under modules/node, installed and updated for you.
modules.needHelp.agent-agy.model: Offered first in the panel. Empty: the first one listed.
modules.needHelp.agent-agy.bin: Path to the agy executable. Empty: the one this installation keeps under modules/node, downloaded from Google and updated for you.
vpn.down: The interface is down: devices connect to nothing, and with their DNS pointing here they lose every name until they disconnect. The house tries to bring it up every 30 seconds; see Events (vpn.down) for why it cannot.
nodes.pickHint: The machine this panel is working on. Everything you do, chats included, happens there.
sites.nodeHint: The machine where the site is made and runs.
dash.sparkLabel: Processor and memory over the last hour
dash.waitsForYou: asked something and waits for an answer
dash.openHint: Move the panel to this node
dash.name: Name
dash.nameHint: How this node appears in the others' panels. Up to 40 characters.
dash.sub: Every node of the network at a glance: its machine, its sites, its conversations and what went wrong lately.
dash.joinBody: Paste the code made in any node of the network (Dashboard → Invite a node). This machine joins the whole network: every node will see and manage every other. The first contact through the tunnel can take up to a minute.
dash.joinEndpointHint: This machine's public IP and the mesh's UDP port, so the others can reach it. Leave it empty if it is behind NAT: it will then always call out first.
dash.createTitle: Create the network and invite a node
dash.createBody: This node is in no network yet: inviting creates one with this node in it. Then paste the code in the other machine (Dashboard → Join a network). It works once, for fifteen minutes.
dash.inviteBody: Paste this code in the other machine (Dashboard → Join a network). It works once, for fifteen minutes, and the machine joins the whole network, not only this node.
dash.endpointHint: Public IP and UDP port of the mesh (51821 by default), as ip:port. That port must be open to the other machines, in this machine's firewall and in the provider's.
dash.alone: This node is in no network.
dash.aloneHint: Invite another machine to create one, or join an existing one with a code made in any of its nodes.
dash.meshError: The mesh is not working on this node:
dash.leaveQ: Take this node out of the network?
dash.leaveBody: The other nodes are told and stop seeing this one; its tunnel goes down. Sites are not touched. Coming back needs a new invitation.
dash.expelBody: Every node stops seeing it and its tunnel is closed everywhere within a minute. Its sites keep running on its machine. Coming back needs a new invitation.
dash.otherVersion: This node runs {v}; this one, {mine}. Update both to the same version.
dash.how1: Every node of the network sees and manages every other: the selector at the top moves this panel to another machine, and everything done there (sites, files, chats, agents) runs on that machine. Joining one node is joining all; a new node appears everywhere within a minute.
dash.how2: The nodes talk only through a WireGuard mesh (UDP 51821): each has a private address in 10.66.0.0/16 and only traffic to another node goes through the tunnel. The rest of each machine's traffic does not change, and through the mesh each node reaches the others' middleware and nothing else of their machines.
dash.how3: Another node can do what an operator can, except change this one's network or touch its passwords, passkeys and tokens: those are decided at each machine's own panel.
system.update.everyHint: How often GitHub is asked for a new release, in whole minutes (1 to 10080). GitHub answers 60 anonymous questions an hour per address: below a few minutes a check can be refused now and then.
system.update.everyBad: A whole number of minutes, from 1 to 10080.
dash.panelVPNOnly: Every node's panel only through a VPN
dash.panelVPNOnlyHint: One decision for every node: no panel of the network answers the internet; each answers through a VPN (its own or another node's) and through the mesh. A node without a VPN of its own is reached from the others. It is turned on from a node with its VPN on and a device in it.
dash.relayHint: With the VPN of any node you reach every node: its resolver answers the other nodes' names and passes their connections, still encrypted, through the mesh. Their panels and their VPN-only sites open as through their own VPN. Way out if no VPN answers: `middleware nodes panel open` on any machine.
dash.panelVPNOnlyQ: Close every node's panel to the internet?
dash.panelVPNOnlyBody: Every panel of the network will answer only through a VPN and the mesh. Make sure your device is connected to a node's VPN and its profile works: from then on it is your way in. If it fails, `middleware nodes panel open` on any machine reopens them.
dash.panelVPNOnlyOn: Every panel answers only through a VPN (the other nodes, within a minute).
dash.panelVPNOnlyOff: Every panel answers the internet again (the other nodes, within a minute).
vpn.panelOnlyNetwork: This node is in a network: the switch applies to every node's panel, and from this node's VPN you reach all of them.

oc.reading: Reading the models of the connected providers…
ban.title: Bans (fail2ban)
ban.sub: Whoever tries to exploit the house or keeps asking for what scanners ask for is cut off in the kernel (nftables, through the helper), for longer at every repeat. Visitors of a site that really has the path (a WordPress's /wp-login.php) are never counted.
ban.onHint: Off, nothing is counted and nobody is banned automatically; the block list keeps working.
ban.what: Banned at once: Log4Shell, climbing out of the folder to /etc/passwd, PHP wrappers, phpunit's eval-stdin, router RCEs, command injection. Counted as an attempt when the site answers with an error: /.env, /.git/, /wp-login.php, /phpmyadmin, .php on a site without PHP… and wrong panel passwords. Never: this machine, private and VPN addresses, the allow list, and an address the operator logged in from in the last week.
oc.popular: The best known (a tap chooses it)
oc.noVendorModels: None yet: they are read with the key when the module is turned on.

access.attackMoved: Under-attack mode is in the Security tab.
security.attack.title: Under attack
security.attack.hint: Every visitor's browser solves a small proof of work before the site is served. It protects nothing: it makes floods expensive. While it is on, what is not a browser (webhooks, API clients, payment callbacks) does not get in unless its path is exempt.
security.attack.offLine: Off. The buttons switch it on with a deadline, or for good.
security.attack.noDeadline: No deadline: it stays on until you switch it off.
security.attack.noSkip: No path is exempt: webhooks and API clients of this site are being turned away.
security.attack.bitsHint: 8 to 24, default 16. Each bit doubles the work: 16 is a fraction of a second, 20 a couple of seconds.
security.attack.skipHint: One prefix per line, by whole segments (/hooks/stripe). Each line is an open door: write the narrowest that works.
security.attack.counts: Since the last restart: {served} challenges served, {solved} solved. Many served and few solved means it is keeping people out, not only a flood.
security.rules.title: Who gets in
security.rules.hint: By what a caller claims to be. The country comes from the edge and can be believed; the User-Agent is written by the caller and can say anything. This clears out what identifies itself (crawlers, scripts), not anyone who insists: Access is for that.
security.bots.title: Robots
security.bots.noUA: Close the door to requests without a User-Agent
security.bots.searchWarn: Closing search engines takes this site out of search results.
security.bots.windowHint: Optional. Daily hours in which the closed families get in anyway (an AI crawler at night, not by day).
security.browsers.title: Browsers
security.countries.title: Countries
security.countries.codesHint: Two letters, comma separated. XX is unknown, T1 is Tor.
security.countries.none: This request arrives with no country: an allow list of countries would shut you out. Turn on IP geolocation at the edge first.
security.agents.title: User-Agent fragments
security.agents.hint: One per line, two characters at least.
security.paths.title: Paths never served
security.paths.hint: One prefix per line, answered 404 before the site sees it (/wp-login.php).
security.messageHint: Empty says why in general terms, never what the rule holds.
security.blocks.title: Last refusals
security.blocks.noneHint: The last 50 requests this site refused show up here, with what they claimed to be. Kept until the next restart.
waf.tripsHint: Floods in one minute that block an address: the address as a whole past eight visitors' worth. A visitor past its own rate only gets 429s, and what a page loads with it costs a quarter. Each block lasts longer than the last.
site.execBody: Runs with sh where the site runs: its folder, its environment and HOME, inside its container if it has one. No input; it is stopped, with everything it started, when the time is up. Every run is recorded as an event.
site.workerStarted: {name} will start on the next tick
site.workerStopBody: It is written to the manifest, so it stays stopped across restarts until you start it again.
manifest.historyHint: Every valid version the house has seen, whoever wrote it: this panel, the API, an agent, a deploy or an editor. The last 50.
manifest.historyRestoreBody: It is validated like a save and applied at once. The version in force now stays in the history, so this can be undone the same way.
activity.trafficHint: Requests per second that reached this site, refreshed every two seconds while this tab is open.
activity.quiet: No requests in the last minute.
activity.noIncidentsHint: What the guard finds about this site shows up here.
access.denyIPsHint: One IP or CIDR per line, refused even when the allow list lets them in. A line that is not an address rejects the whole save.
sites.bulkDeleteBody: Each one is stopped, its names are unpublished, and its folder is archived or deleted:
sites.bulkDeleteTypeWrong: Type the number of sites, {n}, to confirm.
settings.tokenKindScoped: A service door: only some actions
settings.tokenKindHint: A program that only restarts or deploys a site should get a door that does only that.
settings.scope.read: Read sites, their logs and the events
settings.tokenScopeRequired: Choose at least one action, or give it full access.
repos.sub: The git repositories inside the sites. Marked ones are pulled every two minutes: fetch and merge, never reset or force; a merge that collides is undone and shown here. Pulling is not deploying: a site that is built keeps serving the old build until it is deployed.
repos.noneHint: A site folder with a .git, or one up to three levels below it, shows up here.
repos.head: Last commit
repos.autoOff: {where} is no longer pulled by itself
repos.clean: up to date as of the last fetch
auth.passwordClosed: The password is closed on this panel: sign in with a passkey. If you have none, `middleware panel open` on the server opens it for a while.
passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.hint: A passkey signs you in with this device's lock (fingerprint, face, PIN, a security key) and survives a password change. Each one works only on the name it was made on.
passkeys.unsupported: Passkeys need a secure address with a name (https://panel.example, or localhost). Open the panel by its domain to add one.
passkeys.addBody: It will be bound to {host}: it works on this name and no other.
passkeys.name: Name
passkeys.nameRequired: Give it a name to tell it apart.
passkeys.cancelled: The browser's dialog was closed; nothing was done.
passkeys.removeBody: That device will no longer sign in. Sessions already open stay open.
passkeys.noneHint: Add one to sign in without the password, and to have a way in if the password is lost.
panelAccess.title: Who may reach the panel
panelAccess.hint: Addresses or CIDRs, deny first; an allow list with anything in it means only those, loopback included (a site's process is there too). The CLI on the server always gets in, `middleware panel open` lifts the lists from the shell, and a list that would shut you out is refused.
panelAccess.fromMachine: You are on the server's own socket, which always gets in.
panelAccess.allowHint: One per line. An IPv6 address changes by itself every few days: allow its /64.
panelAccess.passkeyOnlyHint: Needs a passkey first; the last passkey cannot be removed while this is on. While opened from the shell (middleware panel open), the password still works.
panelAccess.openNow: Opened from the shell until {at}: these rules do not apply until then.
panelAccess.banner: The panel's address lists and closed password are lifted until {at} (middleware panel open).
push.title: Notifications
push.hint: Pushed to this device even with the panel closed: intrusions, criticals, a repository that stopped pulling, an agent's turn that ended. Choose which, then subscribe.
push.unsupported: This browser cannot receive push notifications here: they need a secure address (https, or localhost) and a browser that supports them. On an iPhone, add the panel to the home screen first.
push.denied: The browser refused notifications for this site; allow them in its settings.
push.noneHint: Subscribe this browser to be told when something needs you.
docs.sub: The documents of this version, as the binary that runs carries them.
audit.sub: What npm's advisory database says about each site's packages, checked daily from its package-lock.json. A critical one that is new is pushed to your devices. Nothing here changes a site's dependencies.
audit.running: Checking every site in the background
audit.noneHint: Sites with a package.json are checked a few minutes after the house starts and then daily.
audit.allClean: No known vulnerabilities in any site.
autofix.title: Automatic repair
autofix.hint: A site that does not start, or stops answering three checks in a row, goes to the house's AI for automatic work (or, with none, to its own agent), which may change its code but not restart it; the house restarts it afterwards. Off until you turn it on here, except for sites that arrived from a move in the last day when there is an AI for automatic work; a site's manifest can say autofix: false.
activity.resourcesHint: Every process of this site added up, its workers' included (containers too), a sample a minute for the last day; pick a worker to see it alone. Five minutes over 90% of a core or 2 GB is an episode.
activity.resourcesNone: No samples yet: the first comes a minute after the site is seen running.
cache.title: House cache
cache.hint: Responses kept in this machine's memory and served without asking the site again, behind the door: nothing passes a password. Answers carry X-Middleware-Cache: hit or miss.
cache.rulesHint: By path prefix, whole segments; the longest wins. Whatever the rules say, nothing with Set-Cookie, private or no-store, and nothing for a request with Authorization, is ever kept.
cache.maxMBHint: Empty: only the house's budget (Settings). It can ask for less, never reserve more.
cache.mode.originHint: Keeps what the site marks with s-maxage or max-age, for as long as it says.
cache.mode.forceHint: Keeps it the seconds given, whatever the site says: for what is public and still.
cache.mode.neverHint: Keeps nothing here, whatever the site says.
edge.sub: Domains to buy, the account's domains, DNS records, Access applications and the Cloudflare token. All but the search need the Cloudflare module.
edge.needsModule: This needs the Cloudflare module, on and with a token that allows it.
edge.searchHint: Asked to each registry by RDAP. Where an ending has none, DNS answers, which cannot tell a free name from one registered and not in use: those say so.
edge.stalePrices: The prices were written on {at} and may have changed since.
edge.mineNone: This Cloudflare account has no domains.
edge.noRegistrarRead: The token cannot read Cloudflare's registrar: expiry and renewal are not shown. Giving it “Registrar Domains Read” fixes it.
edge.name: Name
edge.accessHint: Domains where Cloudflare asks visitors to log in before anything reaches this house.
edge.tokenHint: What the token stored in the Cloudflare module may do, against what the house uses.
edge.wide: It may also: {list}. The house does not use that; a narrower token loses less if it leaks.
edge.narrowAlready: It allows nothing beyond what the house uses.
edge.unreadable: This token may not read its own permissions (it lacks Account API Tokens Read), so they cannot be shown here; everything else works the same. To see them, and to narrow it again, put a token with that permission (the one you had before narrowing, if you did not revoke it) in the Cloudflare module.
edge.missing: The house uses, and this token lacks: {list}.
edge.narrowQ: Replace the token with a narrow one?
edge.narrowBody: A new token with exactly what the house uses is created, checked and stored in place of this one. The current token is not revoked: do it in Cloudflare once the new one has been seen working.
edge.narrowed: Narrow token in use. Revoke the old one ({id}) in Cloudflare.
cache.edgeHint: What Cloudflare keeps at the edge, for names proxied by it. Its rules belong to the zone, not to this site: each says whom it reaches, and the edge takes the first that matches, in this order.
cache.edgePurge: Empty the edge for this site
cache.edgePurged: The edge's cache for this site was emptied
cache.edgeOrdered: Rules that reach this site, in order
cache.edgeAddHint: A path prefix and the seconds the edge keeps it whatever the site says; 0 bypasses the edge there. The rule is born scoped to this site.
cache.edgeOthers: {n} rules of other domains in the zone
cache.edgeDeleteOther: This rule is not this site's ({scope}): deleting it changes how other sites are served, and nothing will say so.
cache.edgeNeedsModule: Needs the Cloudflare module, with a token that may read and write cache rules.
activity.workerNow: Of which worker {name}: {cpu}% of a core, {mem}.

settings.sectionSub.notify: What reaches your devices while the panel is closed.
settings.sectionSub.agents: How many turns run at once, who works when nobody is watching, and the automatic repairs.
settings.sectionSub.access: Who may open the panel, and the tokens scripts use.
settings.sectionSub.browser: Kept in this browser only; the server never sees them.
settings.generalHint: Where this console answers and which ports its sites take.
settings.atRestart: some changes apply at the next restart
autofix.brakesNote: {attempts} attempts per outage · {wait} min apart · up to ${usd} a day
tasks.cron.monthly: On day {days} of every month at {time}
tasks.cronTitle: The schedule as the task writes it (cron)
system.processHint: Where this middleware lives and listens.
llmUse.noSubscriptionHint: A tool signed in with a subscription shows its windows here.
dash.allClearHint: Every site answers, no conversation is waiting and every machine is well.
dash.diskFullHint: {used} of {total} used. Sites and logs stop writing when it fills.
waf.moreRules: Body size, countries and user agents
ban.whatTitle: What is banned at once, and what never is
guard.group.intrusion: The site is stopped at once
guard.groupHint.intrusion: The site is switched off and the process tree is killed; the incident stays here until dismissed.
guard.groupHint.suspicious: An incident and an event; the process keeps running, since it is nearly always explained.
audit.serious: Sites with critical or high vulnerabilities: {n}
sitelist.archiveDeleteBody: It is the last copy of that site, its data included. Once deleted it cannot be restored.
sitelist.noArchivedHint: Deleting a site with “Archive instead” ticked keeps it here, ready to restore.
sitepage.notPublishedHint: Not published yet: nobody outside this machine reaches it by name. Publish points its names here.
sitepage.redirectsNone: No redirects yet. Add one below to send an old address somewhere new.
sitepage.pictureNoneHint: The site as a visitor sees it, renewed while you look at it.
sitepage.pictureOffHint: Taking them needs a headless browser: run the installer with --browser yes.
sitepage.doorNoProcess: Nothing runs here of its own yet, so there is nothing to call the gateway. Give the site a command to run first.
sitepage.cacheNoHitsHint: nothing asked for since the start
security.familyNote.search: Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo. Closing them takes the site out of search results.
security.familyNote.ai: The ones that take the text to train or to answer: GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot.
security.familyNote.social: The ones that fetch the card when a link is pasted. Closing them leaves links without a preview.
security.familyNote.seo: Ahrefs, Semrush and the like. They give the site nothing and ask the most.
security.familyNote.tools: curl, wget, python-requests, headless browsers. Deploy scripts use them too.
security.familyNote.monitors: UptimeRobot, Pingdom and the like. Whoever watches this site from outside is shut out.
security.familyNote.other: Anything that says bot, crawler or spider and is in no table; next month's new names land here.
sitelist.chatAsking: The chat of {domain} is waiting for your answer
tasks.siteSub: Scheduled work that runs in this site's folder, with its environment.
tasks.siteEmptyHint: A task runs a command of {domain} on a schedule: a nightly backup, a cache warm-up, a report.
tasks.siteJsonHint: The task runs in the folder of {domain} with its environment; site is always {domain}.
auth.loginLeadUser: Sign in with the user name and password you were given.
auth.asOwner: I am the owner of this installation
account.signsOut: Every session of yours ends, this one too: you sign in again with the new password.
account.wrongCurrent: The current password is not that one.
sites.emptyMineHint: When the owner of this installation gives you a site, it shows here.
users.title: Users
users.hint: People who manage some sites and nothing else. They sign in on this panel with their name; a site may be on any node of the network, and they never see which.
users.removeBody: Their sessions end now and their name stops working. Their sites stay as they are.
users.name: Name
users.nameHint: 2 to 32 of a-z, 0-9, '.', '_' and '-'. It is what they type to sign in.
users.passwordHint: At least 8 characters. Give it to them yourself; they can change it once inside.
users.newPasswordHint: Leave it empty to keep theirs. A new one ends their sessions.
users.fillIn: A name and a password of at least 8 characters.
users.grantsHint: Each site and what they may do there. Operate shows the site, its logs, files and tasks and restarts, stops, holds and runs tasks; Full management also changes the code, the manifest and the tasks and talks to the agents.
users.fullWarn: Full management runs their code, their tasks and the agents in the site's own jail: they see their site's folder and nothing else of this machine.
users.agents.title: Agents
users.agents.hint: Which agents their conversations may use and, for each, which models. You can pick agents and models this machine does not have yet: the limit applies when they arrive.
users.agents.modelsHint: No model ticked or typed: every model of this agent.
users.agents.none: No agent is known here yet. Turn one on in Modules, or save no agent at all.
tasks.offTitle: Turned off: it does not run on its schedule until it is turned on again
tasks.offNext: does not run on its schedule
site.serviceInside: only the site's other services reach it
site.serviceInternal: no name: only the site's other services reach it
site.serviceStopBody: Its names show the stopped page and the other services keep serving. It is written to the manifest, so it stays stopped across restarts until you start it again.
site.serviceHeldDone: The names of {name} show the holding page
